script: Spread and total were not saved for Week 4 DEN@SF, so this script is form-only from three games. San Francisco's offense is the functional one: Brock Purdy is +1.37 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=25) and +0.39 without, Christian McCaffrey has 166 rush yards on 35 carries plus 104 receiving yards on 17 targets, and George Kittle has 174 yards on 16 targets. Denver is narrower — J.K. Dobbins 121 yards on 35 carries, Jaylen Waddle 150 yards on 21 targets with 247 air yards — and Bo Nix is -0.40 EPA vs blitz (n=31) versus +0.07 with no blitz. Denver's defense is the soft unit at 5.30 rush YPC, 9 runs of 10+, and 11 passes of 20+ on 117 attempts, so the inferred script is SF staying on schedule through McCaffrey and punishing Denver's 38% blitz while Dobbins stalls against SF's 3.79 YPC allowed.
who_goes_off: Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle should go off for San Francisco. McCaffrey's 4.74 YPC on 35 carries meets a Denver front allowing 5.30 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, and his 17 targets for 104 yards are the checkdown when Denver blitzes 38% into Purdy's +1.37 blitz EPA. Kittle's 174 yards and 142 air yards on 16 targets match Denver's middle leak of 8.56 YPA on 16 attempts and 11 allowed passes of 20+.
weak_spot: Denver's real weak spot is the middle and the run front, not the right boundary: middle 8.56 YPA on 16 attempts, left 7.78 on 37, right a firmer 6.04 on 56, plus 5.30 YPC and 9 runs of 10+. That is Kittle/McCaffrey territory, and it also fits Purdy's 94 rush yards on 9 carries. San Francisco's only soft location split is the middle at 7.29 YPA on just 14 attempts; left is 5.74 on 35 and right is 6.45 on 53, with only 4 passes of 20+ on 108 attempts and 3.79 YPC with 3 runs of 10+, so Waddle's 247 air yards and Courtland Sutton's 154 air yards are aimed at the part of the SF defense that has not broken.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for DEN@SF, so no injury fallout is applied — Dobbins's 35 carries, R.J. Harvey's 5 carries and 11 targets, McCaffrey's 35 carries and 17 targets, and Kittle's 16 targets are the usage baseline as given.
qb_vs_blitz: Bo Nix is only a problem if blitzed: -0.40 EPA/dropback vs blitz on 31 dropbacks versus +0.07 with no blitz, and San Francisco blitzes just 26%, so Denver mostly gets the neutral look rather than a collapse or a spike. Brock Purdy is the reverse at +1.37 EPA vs blitz on 25 dropbacks versus +0.39 without, and Denver blitzes 38%, which feeds his 94 rush yards on 9 carries and the quick answers to McCaffrey and Kittle instead of knocking SF off schedule.

picks.why: Brock Purdy has 94 rush yards on 9 carries over three games, 31.3 per game, against a 17.5 line. Denver allows 5.30 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, and their 38% blitz is the look where his EPA/dropback is +1.37 on 25 dropbacks, so scrambles stay in the projection even if 10.4 YPC regresses.

J.K. Dobbins is at 121 yards on 35 carries, 40.3 per game and 3.46 YPC, and the line is 59.5. San Francisco allows 3.79 YPC and only 3 runs of 10+ in three games, so 12 carries at that rate is about 45 yards, and J. Coleman (10 carries) plus R.J. Harvey (5) already split the rest.
